DECEMBER 20, 1938

A large gambling establishment known
as the "Kwang Seng Club," was established
yesterday at 924 Jessfield Road, former
headquarter of the "Tse Seng Shuen Yuen"
Refugee Camp. One SUN SHU CHENG, ex-detective
in the F. S. B. is the leaseholder.

Another gambling den, the "Yuen Tung Club,"

Jessfield Road, the owner being a loafer named
KAO AH KENG.

Date December 14, 1938.

Subject Dah Sung Gambling Den - Employee fired upon by unknown person.

Made by D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by C. Crawford J.

At 9 p.m. December 13, 1938, Ma S-ki (馬士共), who is in charge of a "Yao Tan" gambling table in the Dah Sung Amusement Society (大生娛樂社), 43 Hsing Kong Li, Connaught Road, O.O.L., was fired upon by an unknown person while he was operating the gambling table and wounded in the shoulder. He was immediately sent to hospital, the name of which has not been ascertained, in a private motor car owned by the gambling den in question. The attempted assassin, however, made good his escape during the confusion which followed the shooting.

It is reported that Chih Mo Bi (戚麻皮), proprietor of the Ziang Sung Gambling Den (祥生公司), 70 Zang Shan Li, off Jessfield Road, O.O.L., instigated the shooting. Several days ago, Chih requested Ma S-ki to join his den on account of Ma having a large circle of friends among gamblers and these people would go to gamble where Ma is employed. The request was flatly rejected by Ma with the result that Chih has ever since borne a grudge against him.

Liao Chung Chien
D. S. I.

日期 1938 年 12 月 14 日。

主题 大生赌窟 - 雇员遭不明身份者枪击。

由特别分部副督察廖仲坚呈报，经 J. Crawford 警长转递

1938 年 12 月 13 日晚 9 时，在越界筑路区康纳脱路兴公里 43 号大生娱乐社 (Dah Sung Amusement Society) 负责“摇摊”赌台的马士共 (Ma S-ki)，在操作赌台时遭不明身份者枪击，肩部受伤。他随即被该赌窟的一辆私家车送往医院，医院名称尚未查明。然而，行刺未遂者在枪击后的混乱中成功逃脱。

据报，此次枪击系由越界筑路区极司菲尔路旁脏山里 70 号祥生公司 (Ziang Sung Gambling Den) 业主戚麻皮 (Chih Mo Bi) 唆使。数日前，戚因马士共在赌徒中交友广泛，且这些赌徒会前往马受雇之处赌博，故请求马加入其赌窟。该请求被马断然拒绝，导致戚自此对马怀恨在心。

S. M. C. S.

Date December 1, 38.

Gambling Dens Operating in Extra-Settlement Road Area in
Western District.

Forwarded herewith is an up-to-date list, together
with a map showing the location, of gambling dens operating
in extra-Settlement road area in the Western District.
They number, in all, twenty-two as compared with twenty at
the beginning of November, 1938.

The last numbered one on the list is operated on
the same lines as a foreign gambling house; no person is
admitted if not introduced by a known patron or without
a special introductory card issued by the den owner. The
name of the den is unknown, and it is said, its owner is
one named Li Sui-Kiu (李瑞九), who is the proprietor of
the Li Shu Tuh Tang Broadcasting Station (K.C. 940), 250
Burkill Road. This gentleman is reputed to be wealthy
and has a house at 150 Edinburgh Road where radio broad-
casting is done by remote control from the station in
Burkill Road.

Date November 1, 1938.

Subject Bomb thrown into a gambling den in Western District, O.O.L.

Made by D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by C. **〔此处转录不清〕**

At about 10 p.m. October 31, 1938, a hand-grenade was thrown into the Yung Yuen Gambling Den, 121 Yung Zien Fang, off Lifeng Road, O.O.L., by some unknown person or persons and exploded, injuring eight of the inmates who were conveyed to the Red Cross Hospital, Avenue Haig, for treatment. Two of the injured people are believed to be in a serious condition and are at present detained in the hospital while the remaining six were discharged after treatment.

All local Chinese vernacular newspapers published to-day, November 1, a report on the bomb throwing but only the "Standard" states definitely that the missile exploded in a gambling den, the other papers stating that the incident occurred in a bungalow somewhere in Bubbling Well Road or Edinburgh Road, O.O.L.. The omission by the newspapers of mentioning the gambling den being the target of the bomb thrower would appear to confirm the information contained in a Special Branch report submitted on October 31, 1938, that the editorial staff of the local Chinese vernacular newspapers, with the exception of the "Standard", have agreed to refrain from publishing reports detrimental to the interests of the gambling dens in the Western District, O.O.L..

Liao Chung Chien.

日期 1938年11月1日。

主题 炸弹投入越界筑路区域西区一家赌场。

由 高级情报员 廖仲坚 制作 转发者 C. **〔此处转录不清〕**

1938年10月31日晚10时许，一名或多名不明身份者向位于越界筑路区域立丰路旁永仙坊121号的永源赌场投掷了一枚手榴弹并发生爆炸，致使场内8人受伤，伤者被送往海格大道红十字会医院接受治疗。据信其中两名伤者情况严重，目前仍留院治疗，其余六人在接受治疗后已出院。

今日（11月1日）出版的所有本地中文报纸均报道了这起投弹事件，但只有《标准报》明确指出爆炸物是在一家赌场内爆炸，其他报纸则称事件发生在越界筑路区域静安寺路或爱丁堡路某处的平房内。各报未提及赌场是投弹者的目标，这似乎证实了1938年10月31日提交的一份特别处报告中所载的信息，即除《标准报》外，本地中文报纸的编辑人员已同意不刊登损害越界筑路区域西区赌场利益的报道。

Subject Local Chinese newspapers to refrain from publishing reports
detrimental to the interests of gambling dens in the Western District.
Made by D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by C. Clausen.

Information has been received from a usually reliable
source that an agreement has been reached between the eighteen
gambling dens in the Western District, O.O.L., (Vide list
attached to Special Branch report dated 11/10/38) and the
editorial staff of the following Chinese vernacular newspapers
regarding the publication in future of news reports concerning
the gambling dens:-

1. Sin Wan Pao 2. Shun Pao 3. Hwa Mei Chen Pao
4. Hwa Mei Wan Pao 5. Ta Mei Pao 6. Ta Mei Wan Pao
7. Ta Ying Yeh Pao 8. Kuo Chi Jih Pao 9. Morning Leader
10. News Digest 11. Globe 12. China Evening News
13. Social Daily News 14. Life Daily News 15. Eastern Times.

A gist of the agreement reads as follows:-

1. That the editorial staff of the above newspapers will,
in future, refrain from publishing reports detrimental
to the interests of the gambling dens. They, however,
will not be held responsible for articles of that nature
published in the supplement issues of the papers.

2. That in case a serious incident, in which a gambling den
or dens are involved, occurs and a report on same becomes
absolutely necessary, the editorial staff will publish it
in a mild tone.

3. That each of the eighteen dens contributes $4.00 daily
(totalling $2,160.00 per mensem from the 18 dens) as
remuneration to the editorial staff of the newspapers.

4. That the money be paid in advance but subject to with-
drawal when Items Nos. 1 and 2 are not observed.

During the past month, the number of patrons visiting these gambling dens has █ greatly reduced. The managements on making investigation found that the reports continuously published by local newspapers on brawls, shooting affrays, etc. occurring in the establishments had been the principal cause of the reduction in patronage. They, therefore, approached Sasaki, Chief of the Amusement Supervision Department, 9/470 Yu Yuen Road, for assistance but without successful result, Sasaki intimating that as they were Chinese and the papers were Chinese owned, they should settle the matter among themselves.

Chien Chung Fang (錢忠範), manager of the Yoong Sung Gambling Den, 184 Kong Ka Jao, off Jessfield Road, O.U.L., subsequently contacted Chiang Tsung Nyi (宗義), a reporter of Sin Wan Pao, and through him the above agreement was eventually arrived at.

It will be noted that the "Standard," a strong pro-Chinese newspaper, is not a party to this agreement. The editorial staff of this paper was likewise approached by Chiang Tsung Nyi, but refused to make terms with the gambling dens which are controlled by the Japanese.

The Shanghai Amusement Supervision Department

The Shanghai Amusement Supervision Department
was established by the Japanese Authorities (Military
Gendarmerie) at the end of May, 19--, at No.9, Lane
470, Yu Yuen Road, O.O.L., for the supervision and
control of gambling and Hwo Wei Lottery dens in the
Western District, O.O.L.. One Mr. Sasaki (佐々木),
Japanese, is the officer-in-charge.

All gambling or Hwo Wei Lottery dens operating in
the Western District are required to obtain permits from
the Supervision Department and to pay all fees to this
organ. Establishments failing to apply for permits
or pay the required "fees" are closed by the personnel
of this Department.

There are now 18 gambling dens and approximately
15 Hwo Wei Lottery dens operating in the Western
District with the permission of this Amusement Supervision
Department.

上海游艺监督部

上海游艺监督部由日本当局（军事宪兵队）于19--年5月底在越界筑路区域愚园路470弄9号成立，旨在监管和控制越界筑路区域西区的赌场和花会彩票馆。负责人为一名日本人佐佐木（Sasaki）。

在西区运营的所有赌场或花会彩票馆均需从该监督部获得许可证，并向该机构缴纳所有费用。未能申请许可证或缴纳所需“费用”的场所将被该部门人员关闭。

目前，在该游艺监督部的许可下，西区有18家赌场和约15家花会彩票馆在运营。

Subject Gambling Stalls to start operation in Western District.

Made by D.S.I. Shih Sau-chien Forwarded by C. Crawford. L. I.

Information has been received that since official recognition was given to some twenty gambling dens operating in the Western outside road areas by the Shanghai Amusement Supervision Department, a plan permitting a number of gambling stalls to function in alleyways off the outside roads is now under consideration by this Department. The suggestion was made to the above Department by one Loh Sing Sung (陸雲生) alias Loh Yoong Ziang (陸雲祥), proprietor of the Ting Nyieh Amusement Society, 10 Ting Nyieh Lee, Connaught Road, O.O.L. on behalf of several interested gambling stall conductors. According to arrangements, Loh will be responsible to the Department for the collection of a daily sum of $85.00 as a protection fee and an unlimited number of "Stalls" will be allowed to function. Loh in turn will collect a sum of money on his own behalf from each "Stall" which is operating. Stalls which operate without authority from Loh will be raided by the Department. No fee would will be collected during inclement weather as no gambling will be possible during those days.

It is reported that a large number of those gambling stalls are ready to start operations as soon as the sanction of the Department is obtained.

据获悉，自从上海娱乐监管部正式认可了在西区越界筑路地区运营的约二十家赌场后，该部目前正在考虑一项允许在越界筑路道路的弄堂内设立若干赌博摊档的计划。该建议是由位于西区越界筑路地区康纳脱路鼎业里10号的鼎业游艺社老板陆云生（Loh Sing Sung），又名陆云祥（Loh Yoong Ziang），代表几位相关的赌博摊档经营者向上述部门提出的。根据安排，陆将负责向该部收取每天85.00美元的保护费，并将允许无限数量的“摊档”运营。陆反过来将从每个运营的“摊档”自行收取一笔款项。未经陆授权的摊档将被该部取缔。在恶劣天气期间不收取费用，因为那些日子无法进行赌博。

arrest of these offenders with the exception of a Korean named

All gambling dens at present operating in the Western
outside road areas, have been ordered to temporarily suspend
operations from May 24th, pending re-organization. This order
was issued at 12 noon May 24th by one Mr. Kitaoka (北岡),
Director of the Shanghai Municipal Administrative Office in
the Jessfield Area, through the Chief of the Western Branch
Police Bureau of the above Office, 94 Jessfield Road. A
translation of the order reads as follows:-

" In order to maintain peace and order in the
Western District, all existing gambling dens are hereby
ordered to close from May 24th pending re-organization.
Some of these dens will, however, be selected and allowed
to operate in the near future. Whoever disobeys this order
will be arrested and punished.

The Chief of the Western Branch Police Bureau, Lee
Vee Tseu (李維周) and the Chief of the Western Branch
Detective Corps, Tsang Shu Dien (張書田) are hereby
ordered to carry out the above order without delay.

Kitaoka, Director of the Shanghai Municipal Adminis-
trative Office in the Jessfield Area. May 24th".

It is reported that of the existing gambling dens in
the Western District which number about forty, only fifteen are
in receipt of permission from the Japanese Authorities to
operate. A commission of $1,000 each for a period of ten days
is paid for this permission, but because of the "unauthorized"
gambling dens operating at present, the Japanese Authorities
have decided to re-organize them in order to ensure that only
those who have paid the "fee" are allowed to function.

City Government police under a Japanese officer in plain
clothes attached to the Shanghai Western District Pacifi-
cation Section raided the Dah Sung Gambling Den, situated

negotiation was conducted between Kao Ah Kung and represen-

permission from the latter to run the den. Although some
understanding was reached between them, no official
permission was, however, given at the time the den started

order has been issued this morning, March 18, by the Japanese
Military Police Western Branch Office, 94 Jessfield Road,
instructing all gambling dens hitherto functioning in the
Western District, to cease functioning forthwith, failing
which, the conductors would be summarily arrested and severely
dealt with.

operations, but negotiations aiming at the reopening of such
dens are at present being made by the conductors of these
establishments, with the Japanese Authorities with the help

that the bombing case which recently occurred at the gambling
den, 47 Kong Ka Jao, C.O.L., is the prime factor for such
a decision, although there is a rumour that the Japanese
Authorities have done so in order to obtain further sums of
money as commission for their re-opening.

Subject (in full) Gambling dens in the Western District.

Made by Clerk Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by C Crawford D.S.

The gambling den, Sung Kee Co., situated at 10 Yah Shing Lee, Brenan Road, O.O.L., which was raided by the Dah Dao City Government Police and the Japanese Military Police on March 2, 1938, resumed business on March 3; the persons arrested during the raid, amongst whom were the conductors of the establishment, were released on the night of March 2.

It is reported that the raid was the result of information supplied by one Zee Mung Tsang (徐普春), who bears a personal grudge against Tseu Vung Hai (周文海), one of the principals of the Sung Kee Co.. Zee Mung Tsang conducts a gambling den himself at 15 Zung Zang Lee, off Robison Road, O.O.L. and is believed to be an agent working for the Japanese authorities.

Another gambling den, also with the name of Sung Kee Co., situated at 37 & 38 Shing Kon Lee, off Connaught Road, O.O.L., which was ransacked by some 10 loafers on March 2 and which closed immediately thereafter, resumed operations on March 3 with a new capital of $1,000 reported to have been subscribed by the conductors.

Date March 3, 1938.

Subject Gambling dens in the Western District.

Made by Clerk Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by C. Crawford. D. S.

In addition to the ten gambling dens which have already
been opened in the Western District (Vide Special Branch
reports dated 22/2/38 and 2/3/38) two more were established
at the following addresses on March 2, 1938:-

| Name of Establishment | Address | Conductor |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Sung Kee Co. | 37 & 38, Shing Kong Li, Connaught Rd. O.O.L. | Zee Ven An (徐文安) & Tseu Vung Hai (徐云海), both notorious loafers in the Western District. |
| Name unknown | 5 & 6, San Ming Li, Brenan Road, O.O.L. | Tsang Yu Ding (張雨亭), a loafer in the Western District. |

At about 6 p.m. March 2, 1938, the first mentioned
establishment was raided and robbed by some ten Chinese males,
some of whom were armed with pistols, who succeeded in entering
the premises on the pretext of being bona fide gamblers.
After the robbery the den was closed but it is not known if
it will reopen to business this evening.

At 6.30 p.m. the same evening, a party of Dah Dao City
Government Police, accompanied by several members of the
Japanese Military Police, raided a gambling den also named
Sung Kee Co. at Nos. 10 Yah Shing Lee, off Brenan Road, O.O.L.,
which was formed in February, 1938 under the auspices of Tseu
Vung Hai, one of the conductors of the 1st mentioned establish-
ment (Vide Special Branch report dated 22/2/38). About 50
persons, including the conductors of the establishment, were
arrested whilst all gambling paraphernalia and money were seized.
All the arrested persons are now detained in the Jessfield
Branch of the Dah Dao City Government Police Bureau at 92
Jessfield Road, O.O.L.

由督察（D.I.）潘连璧（Pan Lien-pih）撰写，由督察 C. Crawford 转呈。
位于南市王家角路（Wong Ka Chueh Road）和盐海道115号（115 Yien Hai Road）、由中国游手好闲之徒和日本浪人经营的两家赌博场所，于1938年2月14日迁至以下地址：-
1) 西区孔家宅（Kong Ka Jao）的一栋无门牌号乡间住宅，该地位于极司菲尔路和康纳特路之间。
2) 西区大西路（Great Western Road）（爱丁堡路以东）张家沙（Chang Ka Shah）的一栋乡间住宅。
关于在赌场搬迁前，通过雇佣汽车经中山路将赌客从极司菲尔村运送至南市一事，这些汽车原属于位于南市的汽车行，目前无任何牌照运营，并由赌场经营者雇佣的中国司机驾驶。它们停靠在极司菲尔村外围的地方，但仅停留几分钟便开始返程。
